episodes.188278: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms produced numerous reports of large hail and wind damage.
episodes.188279: Severe thunderstorms moved across the area and off the coast and produced numerous marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.189197: Heavy rain in mid-March brought a period of river flooding to central and southern Arkansas where minor flood stage was recorded on the Fourche LaFave, Saline, and Ouachita River basins.
episodes.189297: A couple of clusters of strong to severe storms moved ESE across GA during the late afternoon and evening hours ahead of a cold front. Gusty winds produced areas of mainly tree and some structure damage.
episodes.189579: A slow-moving, quasi-stationary cold frontal boundary was the focus of strong to severe thunderstorms March 15-16, 2024. A couple of discrete supercell thunderstorms developed off the Mexico plateau during the evening hours of March 15. As the evening/night progressed, these storms formed into a cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms as they translated eastward into and through the Rio Grande Plains and Brush Country of Deep South Texas. In its aftermath, Willacy County proved to be hardest hit as there were reports of nickel size hail, a power pole down, and 55 knot wind gust over Rincon Del San Jose during the overnight hours on March 16. ||Welcome rain fell across the ranch areas north of the populated Lower Rio Grande Valley, but reports indicated that the 3 to 6 inches of rainfall soaked in overnight, leaving no trace of any rural flooding early on March 16th.
episodes.189595: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms moved eastward from the Deep South Texas Brush Country and into Kenedy and Willacy County during the pre-dawn hours of March 16th.  Wind gusts to 55 knots were recorded at the Rincon Del San Jose Texas Coastal Ocean Observing Network (TCOON) site, near the land cut in central Kenedy County over Laguna Madre.
episodes.189857: An upper level low pressure system brought precipitation and thunderstorm impacts to Southern California March 14th through the 16th. The main weather impacts were due to flooding and mountain snow, but a significant amount of lightning was also observed.
episodes.190015: Showers and thunderstorms draped along a cold front in northern Louisiana began racing southeastward late morning on March 15th. Based on local upper air soundings, these storms were moving into an environment with ample mid and upper level instability. In the lower levels, a region of dry air was noted in the midday sounding. That dry slot enhanced downward winds resulting in several severe wind reports across local coastal waters.
episodes.190118: A cold front slowly approaches South Texas from the north, leaving the region in the favorable warm sector with mid-level disturbances aiding in convection. A supercell capable of producing large hail over McMullen and Live Oak Counties occurred during the morning of the 15th. A couple large supercells over eastern Mexico diminished but maintained severe intensity as they moved eastward into Webb County late in the evening of the 15th. Another round of severe storms moved eastward from the Brush Country to the Coastal Plains the night of the 16th into the midday hours of the 17th. A unwarned severe wind gust of 60 mph was reported on the evening of the 15th at KCOT and a golf ball size hail was reported in McMullen County on the morning of the 17th.
episodes.190134: An approaching cold front led to a couple rounds of strong marine thunderstorms across the northwestern Gulf of Mexico during the morning hours of the 16th and then again during the morning and evening hours of the 17th. A strong supercell passed over north of Port Aransas on the morning of the 21st.
episodes.190350: A motocross rider was struck by lightning during a race in Wise County.
episodes.195294: A second, late season, storm rolled across Southwestern California. This storm brought strong north to northeast winds as well as strong thunderstorms with gusty outflow winds  and hail.
